1	//! `deps/llhttp/api.c`: llhttp's public API over its generated parser, ported to Rust.
2	//!
3	//! # The settings
4	//!
5	//! A [`Settings`] is llhttp's table of callbacks, `struct llhttp_settings_s`, which
6	//! `llhttp.h` also names `llhttp_settings_t` and libgit2's `transports/httpparser.h`
7	//! `git_http_parser_settings` ([`SettingsT`], [`HttpParserSettings`]). It has a slot per event
8	//! of a message, each NULL or a callback: a [`Callback`] for an event, such as the start of a
9	//! message or the end of its headers, and a [`DataCallback`] for a run of the input that makes
10	//! up a part of it, such as a header's name or the body. A parser keeps the address of the table
11	//! it is given (`llhttp_init`, [`ParserMut::set_settings`]), and api.c's dispatchers read the
12	//! table on every event of a parse, calling the slot's callback with the parser, or nothing when
13	//! the slot is NULL.
14	//!
15	//! The table owns nothing and holds no context: llhttp's callbacks are handed the parser, whose
16	//! `data` is their context. It keeps its C layout until its `port/layout` stage, since libgit2's
17	//! HTTP client builds one in C, a `static` filled on first use, and hands it to `llhttp_init`.
18	//! A table Rust holds is a plain value, built empty by [`Settings::new`] (`llhttp_settings_init`)
19	//! and filled through [`SettingsMut`]'s setters, one per slot; [`SettingsRef`]'s getters read
20	//! the slots back as the callable types.
21	//!
22	//! # What a table may hold
23	//!
24	//! Each slot is set only from a [`Callback`] or a [`DataCallback`]: a Rust handler behind its
25	//! trampoline, or, inside the crate, a C function that is sound to call with any parser, whatever
26	//! its `data` holds. So every callback of a table Rust builds is sound with every parser, and a
27	//! table installed with [`ParserMut::set_settings`] needs no promise about the parser's `data`:
28	//! that setter is safe, taking a `SettingsRef<'static>`, whose table lives and stays unchanged for
29	//! as long as any parser can keep its address.
30	//!
31	//! A C callback that reads its context through the parser's `data`, as each of libgit2's HTTP
32	//! client's does with its `http_parser_context`, is sound only with the parsers whose `data` it
33	//! expects, so it is no `Callback`, and a table of them is no `Settings` Rust can build. Such a
34	//! table is installed by C, or through the `unsafe` [`ParserMut::set_settings_ptr`], whose caller
35	//! vouches for the parser's `data`, and its callbacks are reached only through the parser that
36	//! holds it, by api.c's dispatchers. That is why the parser's `settings` is read back as the
37	//! address it holds ([`ParserRef::settings_ptr`]), not as a [`SettingsRef`], whose getters
38	//! hand out callbacks callable with any parser.
39	//!
40	//!
41	//! # The parser's API
42	//!
43	//! api.c's functions over a parser are methods of its handles, [`ParserRef`] and
44	//! [`ParserMut`]. Most of them read or write one field, and are that field's accessor in
45	//! `llhttp.rs`, which stands in for both: `llhttp_get_type`, `llhttp_get_method` and
46	//! `llhttp_get_errno` are [`ParserRef::parser_type`], [`ParserRef::method`] and
47	//! [`ParserRef::error`], read as llhttp's enums; `llhttp_get_http_major`,
48	//! `llhttp_get_http_minor`, `llhttp_get_status_code` and `llhttp_get_upgrade` are
49	//! [`ParserRef::http_major`], [`ParserRef::http_minor`], [`ParserRef::status_code`] and
50	//! [`ParserRef::upgrade`]; `llhttp_get_error_reason` and `llhttp_set_error_reason` are
51	//! [`ParserRef::reason`] and [`ParserMut::set_reason`]; and `llhttp_get_error_pos`, whose
52	//! pointer into a past input Rust never follows, is [`ParserRef::error_offset`], which
53	//! locates it in the input it is given. The X-macro generators api.c's name functions
54	//! expand, `HTTP_ERRNO_GEN`, `HTTP_METHOD_GEN` and `HTTP_STATUS_GEN`, turn a map's entry into
55	//! the text its `case` returns, which is [`Errno::constant_name`], [`Method::map_string`]
56	//! and [`Status::map_string`].
57	//!
58	//! What has logic of its own is here: [`ParserMut::execute`] (`llhttp_execute`), the
59	//! pause and its two resumptions ([`ParserMut::pause`], [`ParserMut::resume`],
60	//! [`ParserMut::resume_after_upgrade`]), which move the parser between its running and
61	//! paused states only from the state each expects, the ten lenient setters, each of which
62	//! sets or clears one bit of the lenient flags, and [`ParserRef::debug_trace`]
63	//! (`llhttp__debug`), the trace llhttp's generated parser writes to C's `stderr` when it is
64	//! generated in debug mode, which this build's is not. The parser's lifecycle is here too:
65	//! [`ParserMut::init`] (`llhttp_init`) starts it afresh with a type and a table,
66	//! [`ParserMut::reset`] (`llhttp_reset`) starts it afresh between two connections' messages,
67	//! keeping its type, table, `data` and lenient flags, and [`ParserMut::finish`]
68	//! (`llhttp_finish`) tells it the input has ended. The name functions `llhttp_errno_name`,
69	//! `llhttp_method_name` and `llhttp_status_name` are the maps' [`Errno::constant_name`],
70	//! [`Method::map_string`] and [`Status::map_string`], whose `abort` on a value no entry names
71	//! an enum cannot reach.
72	//!
73	//! # The dispatchers
74	//!
75	//! llhttp's generated parser signals each event of a message through one of api.c's 23
76	//! dispatchers, `llhttp__on_<slot>`, which call the slot of the parser's table of the same
77	//! name with the parser, or return `0` when the parser has no table or the slot is NULL. The
78	//! macro `CALLBACK_MAYBE` makes the 14 that signal an event, such as
79	//! [`ParserMut::on_message_begin`], and `SPAN_CALLBACK_MAYBE` the 9 that hand over a run of the
80	//! input, such as [`ParserMut::on_url`], which also turn the callback's `-1` into `HPE_USER`,
81	//! with the reason `"Span callback error in <slot>"`. They are the parser's methods of the
82	//! same name, each over one of two private functions that stand in for the macros.
83	//!
84	//! The table they read is the one the parser holds, which C may have built of callbacks that
85	//! read the parser's `data` as their context: they reach it through the parser alone, so
86	//! that each callback is called only with the parser whose table holds it, as the contracts
87	//! of [`ParserMut::set_settings_ptr`] and [`ParserMut::set_data`] promise it may be.
88	//!
89	//! # The exports
90	//!
91	//! C outside api.c calls nine of these functions and the 23 dispatchers. libgit2's

136	/// Hands `$then!` api.c's 23 dispatchers, `llhttp__on_<slot>`, in api.c's order within each
137	/// kind: those `SPAN_CALLBACK_MAYBE` makes, which hand a run of the input to a data slot, then
138	/// those `CALLBACK_MAYBE` makes, which signal an event to an event slot. Each is its export's
139	/// name, its slot, which names its method too, and its slot's variant of [`SpanSlot`] or
140	/// [`EventSlot`], with its method's anchor and what it signals. The native methods, the
141	/// region's reads of each slot and the gateway's exports are made from this one list.
142	macro_rules! with_dispatchers {
143	    ($then:ident) => {
144	        $then! {
145	            spans {
146	                /// Replaces `fn::llhttp__on_url`
147	                #[doc(alias = "llhttp__on_url")]
148	                llhttp__on_url, on_url, Url: "a run of a request's URL";
149	                /// Replaces `fn::llhttp__on_status`
150	                #[doc(alias = "llhttp__on_status")]
151	                llhttp__on_status, on_status, Status: "a run of a response's status text";
152	                /// Replaces `fn::llhttp__on_method`
153	                #[doc(alias = "llhttp__on_method")]
154	                llhttp__on_method, on_method, Method: "a run of a request's method";
155	                /// Replaces `fn::llhttp__on_version`
156	                #[doc(alias = "llhttp__on_version")]
157	                llhttp__on_version, on_version, Version: "a run of the message's HTTP version";
158	                /// Replaces `fn::llhttp__on_header_field`
159	                #[doc(alias = "llhttp__on_header_field")]

161	                /// Replaces `fn::llhttp__on_header_value`
162	                #[doc(alias = "llhttp__on_header_value")]

164	                /// Replaces `fn::llhttp__on_body`

251	impl ParserMut<'_> {
252	    /// Parses `data`, the next run of the input, calling the callbacks of the parser's
253	    /// settings as it reads each part of a message: llhttp's entry point, which runs its
254	    /// generated parser, [`parse`](Self::parse), over the run.
255	    ///
256	    /// The parser picks up where the previous run stopped. A pause, by a callback or by
257	    /// [`pause`](Self::pause), or an upgrade stops the run early, at the parser's error
258	    /// position ([`ParserRef::error_offset`]), and each later run returns the same outcome
259	    /// without reading until the parser is resumed.
260	    ///
261	    /// ```
262	    /// use libgit2_crustify::libgit2::deps::llhttp::llhttp::{Parsed, Parser};
263	    ///
264	    /// let mut parser = Parser::new();
265	    /// let response = b"HTTP/1.1 204 No Content\r\n\r\n";
266	    /// assert_eq!(parser.as_mut().execute(response), Ok(Parsed::All));
267	    /// assert_eq!(parser.as_ref().status_code(), 204);
268	    /// ```
269	    ///
270	    /// # Errors
271	    ///
272	    /// The [`ParseError`] the parser stopped at, which it keeps until it is initialised
273	    /// again, as [`parse`](Self::parse) returns it.
274	    ///
275	    /// # Panics
276	    ///
277	    /// As [`parse`](Self::parse): when the parser has no state to run from, where C would
278	    /// abort, and when a callback of the parser's own parse executes it again.
279	    ///
280	    /// Replaces `fn::llhttp_execute`
281	    #[doc(alias = "llhttp_execute")]
282	    pub fn execute(&mut self, data: &[u8]) -> Result<Parsed, ParseError> {
283	        self.parse(data)
284	    }
285	
286	    /// Pauses the parser: a parser with no error takes [`Errno::Paused`], with the reason
287	    /// `"Paused"`, so that its next run returns [`Parsed::Paused`] without reading. A parser
288	    /// that already has an error, a pause among them, keeps it, and its reason.
289	    ///
290	    /// llhttp asks a callback that pauses its parse to return `HPE_PAUSED` rather than call
291	    /// this; libgit2's HTTP client does both at the end of a response's headers. Called from
292	    /// a callback that returns `0`, it leaves the run reading on, and the next run paused.
293	    ///
294	    /// ```
295	    /// use libgit2_crustify::libgit2::deps::llhttp::llhttp::{Errno, Parsed, Parser};
296	    ///
297	    /// let mut parser = Parser::new();
298	    /// parser.as_mut().pause();
299	    /// assert_eq!(parser.as_ref().error(), Ok(Errno::Paused));
300	    /// assert_eq!(parser.as_ref().reason(), Some(c"Paused"));
301	    /// assert_eq!(
302	    ///     parser.as_mut().execute(b"HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\n"),
303	    ///     Ok(Parsed::Paused)
304	    /// );
305	    /// parser.as_mut().resume();
306	    /// assert_eq!(
307	    ///     parser.as_mut().execute(b"HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\n"),
308	    ///     Ok(Parsed::All)
309	    /// );
310	    /// ```
311	    ///
312	    /// Replaces `fn::llhttp_pause`
313	    #[doc(alias = "llhttp_pause")]
314	    pub fn pause(&mut self) {
315	        if self.as_ref().error_raw() != 0 {
316	            return;
317	        }
318	        self.set_error(Errno::Paused);
319	        self.set_reason(Some(c"Paused"));
320	    }
321	
322	    /// Resumes a paused parser: one whose error is [`Errno::Paused`] has it cleared, so that
323	    /// its next run reads on from where it stopped. Any other error, an upgrade's pause
324	    /// among them, stays; the reason stays too.
325	    ///
326	    /// Replaces `fn::llhttp_resume`
327	    #[doc(alias = "llhttp_resume")]
328	    pub fn resume(&mut self) {
329	        self.resume_from(Errno::Paused);
330	    }
331	
332	    /// Resumes a parser paused at an upgrade: one whose error is [`Errno::PausedUpgrade`]
333	    /// has it cleared, so that its next run reads what follows as HTTP again. Any other
334	    /// error stays, and the reason too.
335	    ///
336	    /// ```
337	    /// use libgit2_crustify::libgit2::deps::llhttp::llhttp::{Errno, Parsed, Parser};
338	    ///
339	    /// let mut parser = Parser::new();
340	    /// let upgrade = b"HTTP/1.1 101 Switching Protocols\r\nConnection: upgrade\r\n\
341	    ///                 Upgrade: websocket\r\n\r\n";
342	    /// assert_eq!(parser.as_mut().execute(upgrade), Ok(Parsed::PausedUpgrade));
343	    /// parser.as_mut().resume();
344	    /// assert_eq!(parser.as_ref().error(), Ok(Errno::PausedUpgrade));
345	    /// parser.as_mut().resume_after_upgrade();
346	    /// assert_eq!(parser.as_ref().error(), Ok(Errno::Ok));
347	    /// ```
348	    ///
349	    /// Replaces `fn::llhttp_resume_after_upgrade`
350	    #[doc(alias = "llhttp_resume_after_upgrade")]
351	    pub fn resume_after_upgrade(&mut self) {
352	        self.resume_from(Errno::PausedUpgrade);
353	    }
354	
355	    /// Clears the parser's error when it is `pause`, and leaves it otherwise.
356	    fn resume_from(&mut self, pause: Errno) {
357	        if self.as_ref().error_raw() == pause.raw().cast_signed() {
358	            self.set_error(Errno::Ok);
359	        }
360	    }
361	
362	    /// Sets the lenient flag `flag` when `enabled`, and clears it otherwise, leaving the
363	    /// others as they are.
364	    fn set_lenient(&mut self, flag: u16, enabled: bool) {
365	        let flags = self.as_ref().lenient_flags_raw();
366	        self.set_lenient_flags_raw(if enabled { flags | flag } else { flags & !flag });
367	    }
368	}

370	/// An `llhttp_lenient_flags` bit as the `uint16_t` `lenient_flags` holds it.
371	const fn lenient(flag: sys::llhttp_lenient_flags) -> u16 {
372	    let [low, high, 0, 0] = flag.to_le_bytes() else {
373	        panic!("a lenient flag is wider than `lenient_flags`")
374	    };
375	    u16::from_le_bytes([low, high])
376	}

453	impl ParserRef<'_> {
454	    /// Writes a trace of the parser to C's standard error stream, `stderr`, as llhttp's
455	    /// generated parser does at each step when it is generated in debug mode: the parser's
456	    /// address, its type and flags, the next byte of `rest`, the input still to read (`null`
457	    /// when it is empty), and `msg`, one line in one write:
458	    ///
459	    /// ```text
460	    /// p=0x7ffc3a1c2e40 type=1 flags=00 next=48   debug=on_message_begin
461	    /// ```
462	    ///
463	    /// The line goes through C's stream, in order with what the remaining C writes there.
464	    /// `type` is printed in decimal and the flags and the byte in hexadecimal, two digits at
465	    /// least. A byte of 0x80 or more is printed as two digits, where C, which prints a
466	    /// signed `char` through `%02x`, prints it sign-extended to an `unsigned int`
467	    /// (`ffffff80`), a value `%x` is not defined for.
468	    ///
469	    /// # Errors
470	    ///
471	    /// When `msg` holds a NUL byte, which C's stream cannot carry, or the write fails, as
472	    /// [`FileRef::print`](glibc_bindings::libc::libio::genops::FileRef::print) reports it.
473	    ///
474	    /// Replaces `fn::llhttp__debug`
475	    #[doc(alias = "llhttp__debug")]
476	    pub fn debug_trace(&self, rest: &[u8], msg: &str) -> io::Result<()> {
477	        ffi_import::print_to_stderr(&self.debug_line(rest, msg))
478	    }
479	
480	    /// The line [`debug_trace`](Self::debug_trace) writes, its newline included.
481	    ///
482	    /// It is built from its parts, without `format_args!`, whose expansion holds an
483	    /// `unsafe` block outside the module's regions.
484	    fn debug_line(&self, rest: &[u8], msg: &str) -> String {
485	        let mut line = String::from("p=0x");
486	        push_hex(&mut line, self.as_ptr().addr(), 1);
487	        line.push_str(" type=");
488	        line.push_str(&self.parser_type_raw().to_string());
489	        line.push_str(" flags=");
490	        push_hex(&mut line, usize::from(self.flags_raw()), 2);
491	        match rest.first() {
492	            None => line.push_str(" next=null"),
493	            Some(&next) => {
494	                line.push_str(" next=");
495	                push_hex(&mut line, usize::from(next), 2);
496	                line.push_str("  ");
497	            }
498	        }
499	        line.push_str(" debug=");
500	        line.push_str(msg);
501	        line.push('\n');
502	        line
503	    }
504	}
505	
506	/// Appends `value` in lowercase hexadecimal, at least `digits` digits, zero-padded, as
507	/// printf's `%0<digits>x` and `%p`'s digits print it.
508	fn push_hex(line: &mut String, value: usize, digits: usize) {
509	    let width = usize::try_from(value.bit_width().div_ceil(4)).unwrap_or(digits);
510	    for i in (0..width.max(digits)).rev() {
511	        let nibble = (value >> (i * 4)) & 0xF;
512	        line.push(char::from(b"0123456789abcdef"[nibble]));
513	    }
514	}

550	    /// events to `settings`: as [`reinit`](Self::reinit) leaves it, every field zero but its
551	    /// start state, `data` included, then its type and its table stored, which `reset` keeps.
552	    ///
553	    /// ```
554	    /// use libgit2_crustify::libgit2::deps::llhttp::api::Settings;
555	    /// use libgit2_crustify::libgit2::deps::llhttp::llhttp::{Parsed, Parser, ParserType};
556	    ///
557	    /// static SETTINGS: std::sync::LazyLock<Settings> = std::sync::LazyLock::new(Settings::new);
558	    ///
559	    /// let mut parser = Parser::new();
560	    /// parser
561	    ///     .as_mut()
562	    ///     .init(ParserType::Request, Some(SETTINGS.as_ref()));
563	    /// assert_eq!(parser.as_ref().parser_type(), Ok(ParserType::Request));
564	    /// assert_eq!(
565	    ///     parser.as_mut().execute(b"GET / HTTP/1.1\r\n\r\n"),
566	    ///     Ok(Parsed::All)
567	    /// );
568	    /// ```
569	    ///
570	    /// # Panics
571	    ///
572	    /// As [`reinit`](Self::reinit): when a callback of the parser's own parse calls it.
573	    ///
574	    /// Replaces `fn::llhttp_init`
575	    #[doc(alias = "llhttp_init")]
576	    pub fn init(&mut self, parser_type: ParserType, settings: Option<SettingsRef<'static>>) {
577	        self.reinit();
578	        self.set_parser_type(parser_type);
579	        self.set_settings(settings);
580	    }
581	
582	    /// Initialises the parser again, in place, as [`init`](Self::init) does, but keeping its
583	    /// type, its table, its `data` and its lenient flags: for the next message of another
584	    /// input, with the parser's error, reason and the state of its message cleared.
585	    ///
586	    /// ```
587	    /// use libgit2_crustify::libgit2::deps::llhttp::llhttp::{Parsed, Parser, ParserType};
588	    ///
589	    /// let mut parser = Parser::new();
590	    /// parser.as_mut().init(ParserType::Response, None);
591	    /// parser.as_mut().set_lenient_version(true);
592	    /// assert!(parser.as_mut().execute(b"GET / HTTP/1.1\r\n").is_err());
593	    /// parser.as_mut().reset();
594	    /// assert_eq!(parser.as_ref().parser_type(), Ok(ParserType::Response));
595	    /// assert_eq!(parser.as_ref().reason(), None);
596	    /// assert_eq!(
597	    ///     parser.as_mut().execute(b"HTTP/3.7 200 OK\r\n"),
598	    ///     Ok(Parsed::All)
599	    /// );
600	    /// ```
601	    ///
602	    /// # Panics
603	    ///
604	    /// As [`reinit`](Self::reinit): when a callback of the parser's own parse calls it.
605	    ///
606	    /// Replaces `fn::llhttp_reset`
607	    #[doc(alias = "llhttp_reset")]
608	    pub fn reset(&mut self) {
609	        let parser_type = self.as_ref().parser_type_raw();
610	        let lenient_flags = self.as_ref().lenient_flags_raw();
611	        self.reinit_keeping_context();
612	        self.set_parser_type_byte(parser_type);
613	        self.set_lenient_flags_raw(lenient_flags);
614	    }
615	
616	    /// Tells the parser that its input has ended, as at the close of the connection it reads.
617	    /// A message whose end only the input's marks, such as a response with neither a
618	    /// `Content-Length` nor chunks, ends here, and its table's `on_message_complete` runs.
619	    ///
620	    /// The outcome follows the parser's `finish` state, which its parse keeps: between two
621	    /// messages, or inside one that needs nothing more, the input may end, and the parser
622	    /// finishes; inside a message whose end must be read, it may not.
623	    ///
624	    /// A parser that has an error, a pause among them, finishes at once, without a callback,
625	    /// and keeps its error.
626	    ///
627	    /// ```
628	    /// use libgit2_crustify::libgit2::deps::llhttp::api::FinishError;
629	    /// use libgit2_crustify::libgit2::deps::llhttp::llhttp::{Parsed, Parser};
630	    ///
631	    /// let mut parser = Parser::new();
632	    /// let response = b"HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\n\r\nthe body runs to the end of the input";
633	    /// assert_eq!(parser.as_mut().execute(response), Ok(Parsed::All));
634	    /// assert_eq!(parser.as_mut().finish(), Ok(()));
635	    ///
636	    /// parser.as_mut().reinit();
637	    /// assert_eq!(parser.as_mut().execute(b"HTTP/1.1 200"), Ok(Parsed::All));
638	    /// assert_eq!(parser.as_mut().finish(), Err(FinishError::InvalidEofState));
639	    /// assert_eq!(parser.as_ref().reason(), Some(c"Invalid EOF state"));
640	    /// ```
641	    ///
642	    /// # Errors
643	    ///
644	    /// [`FinishError::InvalidEofState`] when the input ended inside a message, with the
645	    /// reason `"Invalid EOF state"`, and [`FinishError::Callback`] when `on_message_complete`
646	    /// returned a value other than `0`. The parser's error is left as it was.
647	    ///
648	    /// # Panics
649	    ///
650	    /// When the parser's `finish` state is no `llhttp_finish`, as only
651	    /// [`set_finish_raw`](Self::set_finish_raw) stores, where C would abort.
652	    ///
653	    /// Replaces `fn::llhttp_finish`
654	    #[doc(alias = "llhttp_finish")]
655	    pub fn finish(&mut self) -> Result<(), FinishError> {
656	        // We're in an error state. Don't bother doing anything.
657	        if self.as_ref().error_raw() != 0 {
658	            return Ok(());
659	        }
660	        match u32::from(self.as_ref().finish_raw()) {
661	            sys::HTTP_FINISH_SAFE_WITH_CB => {
662	                match NonZero::new(self.callback_maybe(EventSlot::MessageComplete)) {
663	                    None => Ok(()),
664	                    Some(code) => Err(FinishError::Callback(code)),
665	                }
666	            }
667	            sys::HTTP_FINISH_SAFE => Ok(()),
668	            sys::HTTP_FINISH_UNSAFE => {
669	                self.set_reason(Some(c"Invalid EOF state"));
670	                Err(FinishError::InvalidEofState)
671	            }
672	            _ => panic!("the llhttp parser's finish state is no `llhttp_finish`"),
673	        }
674	    }
675	}

677	/// Why [`ParserMut::finish`] refused the end of the input, as `llhttp_finish` reports it: an
678	/// `llhttp_errno_t` other than `HPE_OK`, which the parser does not keep as its error.
679	#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
680	pub enum FinishError {
681	    /// `HPE_INVALID_EOF_STATE`: the input ended inside a message whose end must be read,
682	    /// such as one whose `Content-Length` it had not reached.
683	    InvalidEofState,
684	    /// The value `on_message_complete` returned, ending the message the input's end ended:
685	    /// `-1` for an error, `HPE_PAUSED` for a pause, or any other.
686	    Callback(NonZero<c_int>),

696	            Self::Callback(code) => code.get(),
697	        }

# The gateway's handles claim of C's parsers more than C keeps

- **finding**: `contracts/ffi_export/gateway-handles-claim-more-than-c-keeps`
- **batch**: `wave-194/batch-6/run-1`, the `symbol` review of `deps/llhttp/api.c`'s folded
  waves
- **items**: api.c's exports under `ffi-export-deps-llhttp-api-c` (`fn::llhttp_execute`,
  `fn::llhttp_finish`, the 23 `fn::llhttp__on_<slot>` and the others built on `parser_mut`),
  and `ffi_import`'s `ParserMut::table`, which the dispatchers read
- **affected commit**: `b3d6b9b37` (`parser_mut` since `2a51ccb3f`)
- **files**: `src/libgit2/deps/llhttp/api.rs`

## Finding

Every export but `llhttp_get_error_pos` and `llhttp_get_error_reason` builds its parser's
exclusive handle with `parser_mut`, whose `// SAFETY:` comment vouches for the handle's
invariant on this ground:

> its `settings` and `data` meet `set_settings_ptr`'s and `set_data`'s contracts, which is
> what C's own callers of `llhttp_execute` promise

and `table()`'s comment counts "C's callers of api.c's functions with their own tables" among
those that meet `set_settings_ptr`'s contract "for as long as the parser holds it". Since
`b3d6b9b37`, those contracts ask that the table's callbacks be sound with the parser's `data`
*at any time* while the parser holds the table, since the dispatchers are safe methods. C's
callers promise no such thing. libgit2's HTTP client, the only C that calls these exports
with a table, installs a `static` table once (`reset_parser`, `llhttp_init`,
`c/src/libgit2/transports/httpclient.c:917-922`), points `data` at a stack
`http_parser_context` only around its own parses, and sets it NULL again before returning
(`httpclient.c:1271`/`1283`, `1458`/`1473`, `1503`/`1529`, `1548`/`1565`). Its callbacks
dereference `data` unconditionally (`on_header_complete`, `httpclient.c:161-165`, and the
others at `228`, `263`, `351`, `395`, `417`). Between those calls a dispatcher would follow
NULL.

The exports are nonetheless sound: each builds its handle for its own call, uses it for that
call's one operation and drops it before returning, and during the call C's caller keeps its
table and its context, as llhttp asks of it. So the invariant the comments claim does not
hold, but the one the code needs does. A justification resting on what C does not promise is
a contracts finding; no reproducer is needed, since nothing unsound is reachable.

## Fix

In this batch's second commit, `parser_mut`'s `// SAFETY:` comment rests the handle's
invariant on its confinement: the handle's lifetime is the export's call, for which C's
caller keeps its table and the context its callbacks read, and no longer, as
`httpclient.c`'s NULL `data` between calls shows, so no handle over a C parser may outlive
the call that builds it. `table()`'s comment says the same of a handle the gateway builds.
The code does not change.
# `set_settings_ptr` and `set_data` bound their obligations by later safe calls

- **finding**: `contracts/ffi_import/settings-ptr-bounds-a-table-by-later-safe-calls`
- **batch**: `wave-194/batch-6/run-1`, the `symbol` review of `deps/llhttp/api.c`'s folded
  waves, over `wave-194/batch-1` (`2c69341c3`), `wave-194/batch-3` (`2a51ccb3f`) and
  `wave-194/batch-4` (`b3d6b9b37`)
- **items**: `fld::llhttp__internal_s.settings` (`ParserMut::set_settings_ptr`),
  `fld::llhttp__internal_s.data` (`ParserMut::set_data`), whose contracts batch 4 widened for
  the 23 dispatchers it made safe (`fn::llhttp__on_url` and the others, `ParserMut::on_url`…)
- **affected commit**: `b3d6b9b37`
- **files**: `src/libgit2/deps/llhttp/llhttp.rs`, `src/libgit2/deps/llhttp/api.rs`

## Finding

Batch 4 made api.c's dispatchers the parser's safe methods: `ParserMut::on_url(&[u8])`,
`on_message_complete()` and the 21 others read the table the parser's `settings` addresses
and call the slot's callback with the parser, at any time, not only from a parse
(`src/libgit2/deps/llhttp/api.rs`, `ffi_import`'s `table`, `call_event`, `call_span`). It
widened the two `unsafe` setters' contracts for them, but kept their duration as a span of
*execution*:

- `set_settings_ptr`: the table "stays live and unchanged, and whose callbacks are sound to
  call with this parser and its `data`, for as long as the parser executes with it: api.c's
  dispatchers read it on every event of `llhttp_execute` and `llhttp_finish`";
- `set_data`: "while the parser executes with those settings, `data` must be what they
  expect", the parser executing "whenever one of its parses, its `finish` or one of api.c's
  dispatchers … calls them, which the safe API allows at any time".

An obligation bounded by when the parser *executes* is one that later safe code, not the
`unsafe` caller, decides the end of: a caller who keeps the table for every parse and finish
it runs, and frees it once it has done executing the parser, reads the first sentence as
satisfied, yet any safe code that later holds the parser calls a dispatcher, which reads the
freed table. What the dispatchers rely on is what `table()`'s `// SAFETY:` comment states, and
the contract did not: that the table lives and stays unchanged "for as long as the parser
holds it", until it is replaced or the parser is initialised again (`reset` keeps it). The
same holds of `data` beside a table whose callbacks read it.

## Evidence

# The gateway's handles claim of C's parsers more than C keeps

- **finding**: `contracts/ffi_export/gateway-handles-claim-more-than-c-keeps`
- **batch**: `wave-194/batch-6/run-1`, the `symbol` review of `deps/llhttp/api.c`'s folded
  waves
- **items**: api.c's exports under `ffi-export-deps-llhttp-api-c` (`fn::llhttp_execute`,
  `fn::llhttp_finish`, the 23 `fn::llhttp__on_<slot>` and the others built on `parser_mut`),
  and `ffi_import`'s `ParserMut::table`, which the dispatchers read
- **affected commit**: `b3d6b9b37` (`parser_mut` since `2a51ccb3f`)
- **files**: `src/libgit2/deps/llhttp/api.rs`

## Finding

Every export but `llhttp_get_error_pos` and `llhttp_get_error_reason` builds its parser's
exclusive handle with `parser_mut`, whose `// SAFETY:` comment vouches for the handle's
invariant on this ground:

> its `settings` and `data` meet `set_settings_ptr`'s and `set_data`'s contracts, which is
> what C's own callers of `llhttp_execute` promise

and `table()`'s comment counts "C's callers of api.c's functions with their own tables" among
those that meet `set_settings_ptr`'s contract "for as long as the parser holds it". Since
`b3d6b9b37`, those contracts ask that the table's callbacks be sound with the parser's `data`
*at any time* while the parser holds the table, since the dispatchers are safe methods. C's
callers promise no such thing. libgit2's HTTP client, the only C that calls these exports
with a table, installs a `static` table once (`reset_parser`, `llhttp_init`,
`c/src/libgit2/transports/httpclient.c:917-922`), points `data` at a stack
`http_parser_context` only around its own parses, and sets it NULL again before returning
(`httpclient.c:1271`/`1283`, `1458`/`1473`, `1503`/`1529`, `1548`/`1565`). Its callbacks
dereference `data` unconditionally (`on_header_complete`, `httpclient.c:161-165`, and the
others at `228`, `263`, `351`, `395`, `417`). Between those calls a dispatcher would follow
NULL.

The exports are nonetheless sound: each builds its handle for its own call, uses it for that
call's one operation and drops it before returning, and during the call C's caller keeps its
table and its context, as llhttp asks of it. So the invariant the comments claim does not
hold, but the one the code needs does. A justification resting on what C does not promise is
a contracts finding; no reproducer is needed, since nothing unsound is reachable.

## Fix

In this batch's second commit, `parser_mut`'s `// SAFETY:` comment rests the handle's
invariant on its confinement: the handle's lifetime is the export's call, for which C's
caller keeps its table and the context its callbacks read, and no longer, as
`httpclient.c`'s NULL `data` between calls shows, so no handle over a C parser may outlive
the call that builds it. `table()`'s comment says the same of a handle the gateway builds.
The code does not change.
# `set_settings_ptr` and `set_data` bound their obligations by later safe calls

- **finding**: `contracts/ffi_import/settings-ptr-bounds-a-table-by-later-safe-calls`
- **batch**: `wave-194/batch-6/run-1`, the `symbol` review of `deps/llhttp/api.c`'s folded
  waves, over `wave-194/batch-1` (`2c69341c3`), `wave-194/batch-3` (`2a51ccb3f`) and
  `wave-194/batch-4` (`b3d6b9b37`)
- **items**: `fld::llhttp__internal_s.settings` (`ParserMut::set_settings_ptr`),
  `fld::llhttp__internal_s.data` (`ParserMut::set_data`), whose contracts batch 4 widened for
  the 23 dispatchers it made safe (`fn::llhttp__on_url` and the others, `ParserMut::on_url`…)
- **affected commit**: `b3d6b9b37`
- **files**: `src/libgit2/deps/llhttp/llhttp.rs`, `src/libgit2/deps/llhttp/api.rs`

## Finding

Batch 4 made api.c's dispatchers the parser's safe methods: `ParserMut::on_url(&[u8])`,
`on_message_complete()` and the 21 others read the table the parser's `settings` addresses
and call the slot's callback with the parser, at any time, not only from a parse
(`src/libgit2/deps/llhttp/api.rs`, `ffi_import`'s `table`, `call_event`, `call_span`). It
widened the two `unsafe` setters' contracts for them, but kept their duration as a span of
*execution*:

- `set_settings_ptr`: the table "stays live and unchanged, and whose callbacks are sound to
  call with this parser and its `data`, for as long as the parser executes with it: api.c's
  dispatchers read it on every event of `llhttp_execute` and `llhttp_finish`";

  expect", the parser executing "whenever one of its parses, its `finish` or one of api.c's
  dispatchers … calls them, which the safe API allows at any time".

An obligation bounded by when the parser *executes* is one that later safe code, not the
`unsafe` caller, decides the end of: a caller who keeps the table for every parse and finish
it runs, and frees it once it has done executing the parser, reads the first sentence as
satisfied, yet any safe code that later holds the parser calls a dispatcher, which reads the
freed table. What the dispatchers rely on is what `table()`'s `// SAFETY:` comment states, and
the contract did not: that the table lives and stays unchanged "for as long as the parser
holds it", until it is replaced or the parser is initialised again (`reset` keeps it). The

api.c's last `port` batch, the `symbol` route of waves 195 and 196: 32 items in
`src/libgit2/deps/llhttp/api.rs`. `fn::llhttp_init` is `ParserMut::init(ParserType,
Option<SettingsRef<'static>>)`, over `reinit`, `set_parser_type` and `set_settings`;
`fn::llhttp_reset` is `ParserMut::reset()`, which keeps the type byte, the table, `data` and the
lenient flags across `reinit`, so a parser of both kinds keeps the type its first message
settled; `fn::llhttp_finish` is `ParserMut::finish() -> Result<(), FinishError>`, where
`FinishError` is `InvalidEofState` (with C's reason `"Invalid EOF state"`) or
`on_message_complete`'s own non-zero value, `HPE_PAUSED` included, neither kept as the parser's
error, as C keeps neither. A parser with an error finishes at once, as C's does, and a finish
state no `llhttp_finish` names panics where C aborts. `fn::llhttp_settings_init` keeps batch 2's
`Settings::new()`, now native, the zeroed table its `memset` leaves; its anchor moved from
`Wraps` to `Replaces`. The name functions `llhttp_errno_name`, `llhttp_method_name` and
`llhttp_status_name` are each a `switch` of the cases batch 3's generators stand for, so they
are ported onto `Errno::constant_name`, `Method::map_string` and `Status::map_string`, which
carry a third anchor each (`crustify/evolution/port-onto-an-existing-accessor`, with this
evidence); their `default: abort()` no enum reaches.

The 23 dispatchers are one table, `with_dispatchers!`, from which the native methods, the
region's slot reads and the gateway's exports are made. `mac::CALLBACK_MAYBE` and
`mac::SPAN_CALLBACK_MAYBE` are the private `callback_maybe(EventSlot)` and
`span_callback_maybe(SpanSlot, &[u8])`, the stringified `#NAME` a per-slot `&'static CStr` made
at compile time; each `fn::llhttp__on_<slot>` is the public `ParserMut::on_<slot>()` or
`on_<slot>(&[u8])` over them, returning C's `int`, which `llhttp.c`'s port will call. A
dispatcher reads the table the parser holds through `ffi_import` alone: the region maps a slot
to its field and calls what it holds with the parser, so that a C table, whose callbacks read
`data`, is still only called with its own parser. The dispatchers being safe,
`set_settings_ptr`'s and `set_data`'s contracts now say that the callbacks they vouch for may be
called at any time while the parser holds them, in any order, with any run. `reset` restores
`data` and `settings` through `ffi_import`'s `reinit_keeping_context`, and the type byte, as C
stores an unnamed `llhttp_type_t`, through `set_parser_type_byte`. `init` and `reset` panic, as
`reinit` does, from a callback of their parser's own parse; the dispatchers and `finish` do
not need to, since they leave where the parse stands. libc's `abort` and `memset` keep their
`std` route: the zeroed value for `memset`, `std::process::abort` in `llhttp_init`'s gateway,
which cannot fail, and a panic where `llhttp_finish` aborts, reported as `HPE_INTERNAL` by its
export, as `llhttp_execute`'s is.

checked against their raw bindings. No header declares the dispatchers, which `llhttp.c`
declares for itself, so they have no raw binding: each is checked against a function-pointer
type transcribed from `llhttp.c`'s prototype, and the `equiv` tests reach api.c's C through an

raw bindings gain `llhttp_finish`'s enum, the `HTTP_FINISH_*` states `finish` matches. The five

  reproducer that keeps to both `unsafe` setters' contracts sets a reason its context owns, frees
  the context once the parser is done, and then reads freed memory through `reason()` (ASan
  heap-use-after-free). The contract now asks that such a reason stay live and unchanged while
  the parser holds it, and `Callback::from_fn`'s that a reason its function sets live as long as
  the program. `reason`'s `SAFETY` comment and the module documentation name both. The
  regression test is `ub_unsafe`'s
  `set_settings_ptr::a_reason_its_callbacks_set_is_read_while_the_parser_holds_it`.

What held. `set_settings(Option<SettingsRef<'static>>)` did not break. A local table and a leaked
`&'static mut` written afterwards are refused at compile time (batch 2's compile-fail
doctests), a `Mutex` guard lends its table only for the guard's borrow, and a table replaced or
cleared mid-parse is sound (batch 2's `ub_safe` tests). C reads a table only through `const llhttp_settings_t *`
(`api.c`'s `CALLBACK_MAYBE`, `llhttp_reset`). `Settings`' `Send` and `Sync` hold, since its slots
are `Callback` and `DataCallback` function pointers and nothing writes it through a shared
borrow. `data` and the `settings` getter stay raw addresses with good reason: a handle may
address a parser whose table C built, whose callbacks read `data` as their context. So a safe
`set_data`, or a `SettingsRef` read back from a parser, would hand C a context it does not expect.
The cost is that a Rust handler reaches per-parser context only through `unsafe` or a
thread-local; no primitive expresses a context reached through an argument yet. The six
private fields without an accessor are touched by `llhttp.c`'s generated code alone. A grep
of `api.c`, `http.c`, `transports/httpclient.c`, `httpparser.c`/`.h` and the C tests confirms
it, so `wrap-ahead-field-users` stands. The setters cannot reach the generated parser's
`abort` either, since `s_error` is `0` and `parse` refuses a parser with a NULL `_current`.

content.content:
The campaign's first switch, run by `modules/libgit2/src/util/utf8.c/integration/run-1` on the
module's branch after the merge of the working branch (`43605086f`): `012d1d34c`, and the
fork's `1b37e3d08`. The export feature `ffi-export-src-util-utf8-c` is deleted, the crate's
only one, so `utf8.rs`'s gateway compiles from now on, and its four `unit_priv` tests run in
`lib`. The module's six `equiv` tests are retired with the C they compared
(`tests/equiv/src/util/utf8.rs`); their cases stay in its unit tests and doctests. The raw
bindings of `git_utf8_iterate`, `git_utf8_char_length` and `git_utf8_valid_buf_length` stay,
and now reach the exports. `src/util/utf8.c` leaves `c/`: the change is the commit
`integrate src/util/utf8.c` on a local `fork/main`, which stands for
`crustify-rs/libgit2-fork`'s `main` and is not pushed, and `.gitmodules` names the fork.
`utf8.h` stays for `path.c`, `diff_xdiff.c` and `fs_path.c`. The module's tied C test,
`tests/util/utf8.c`, calls `git_utf8_char_length` alone, so it stays and checks the export.
No C test leaves, so no case needs listing. The exports are a private module's, so the
crate's API does not change.

The switch also made the one-time change of the C build. The fork's
`cmake/SelectRust.cmake` links the static library that `LIBGIT2_RUST_LIBRARY` names wherever
the remaining C is linked: `libgit2.so`, the CLI, `libgit2_tests` and `util_tests`. It is an
imported target among `LIBGIT2_SYSTEM_LIBS`. `libgit2.so` keeps the Rust's symbols local
(`--exclude-libs`). Its dynamic symbols are the previous generation's on every variant,
`asan-ubsan`'s two linker-made `__start_`/`__stop_asan_globals` aside. Those come from LLVM
23's instrumentation of the Rust and are protected. Without the variable, the library leaves
the three exports undefined, as the crate's bundled and shared builds of `c/` need. Each
variant's `build` command first makes the library (`crustify/scripts/rust-staticlib.sh`),
between `configure` and the C's link. It builds the crate of the checkout that runs it as a
`staticlib` on the dev profile, the profile the Rust tests run on, so that the C tests check
the same build with debug assertions and overflow checks on. It builds in campaign mode
against the configured variant, with `--features bindgen`, so that the committed bindings
are checked, and with `CRUSTIFY_STATICLIB`, under which `build.rs` reads the build's
configuration and links none of its C. It instruments the Rust as `cargo-variant.sh` does.
`nm` shows that the library defines only the Rust, the three exports and the crate's
`__extern` wrappers, and no libgit2 C. Every other campaign build leaves the library out of
its link, matched by canonical path, so that no binary holds the Rust twice. BSan has no
`cargo bsan rustc`, so a stand-in for the cargo it runs turns its `build` into `rustc
--crate-type staticlib`. The BSan runtime its driver bundles is removed from the copy, since
the variant's C link links it.

The variants were rebuilt as a new generation, `crustify/builds.gen1`, with
`crustify/scripts/build-variants.sh`, and this worktree's `crustify/builds` links to it.
`crustify/builds` itself, which three batches were using, was left untouched. Each variant is
configured from the generation's own `c`, a detached worktree of the fork at `1b37e3d08`, so
that the build outlives this worktree and the base checkout's next moves (`build.json`
version 7). Each archive holds 212 objects, where the previous generation's held 213:
`utf8.c.o` is gone. Each variant passed its smoke test (`util_tests -sutf8`). In every
variant, `utf8proc_utf8class` is absent from the C test executables, which take
`git_utf8_iterate` from the Rust; in `libgit2.so` it is a local symbol.

Gates on `012d1d34c`, over gen1, from `end-gates` snapshots at 24 jobs. The workspace is
formatted, and `clippy --workspace --all-targets` passes with warnings denied. Plain passes
the whole workspace: `lib` 848 and 1 ignored, `equiv` 528, `ub_safe` 763, `ub_unsafe` 120,
`unit_pub` 84, `hidden_symbols` 1, doctests 76 and 378. ASan+UBSan and TSan pass it but for
the known nightly failures: the 9 `compile_fail` snapshots and the `CommitBuilder` doctest
(E0624). Miri passes every binary: `lib` 400, `ub_safe` 194, `equiv` 38, `unit_pub` 49,
`ub_unsafe` 19, the rest marked. The remaining C tests ran over the link with the Rust,
through `crustify/scripts/c-tests.sh`. It runs `build.json`'s `ctest` command, then every
suite alone as the baseline did, and compares the result with `c-baseline.json`. Plain,
ASan+UBSan and TSan give 3443 passed and 55 skipped of 3498, coverage 3444 and 54, each the
baseline's record. Under TSan, the same 10 suites as the baseline's report the C's
lock-order inversions and races, and no case fails; no report has a Rust frame. `ctest`
passes both targets on plain, ASan+UBSan and coverage. Under TSan it fails `offline` on those
reports alone, 49 lock-order inversions and glibc's `tzset` race. BSan was rebuilt and not
run, as the settings' `sanitizers` answer has it. `c/` changed, so the crate was packaged as
`package-gate-procedure` has it. The package has 697 files, `utf8.c` out and
`SelectRust.cmake` in, and builds alone in bundled mode. Its `libgit2.pc`'s
`Requires.private` also needs the side campaigns' installs on `PKG_CONFIG_PATH`, beside

content.content:
## Legend

- `module` / `wave` / `batch` — the batch's place in `schedule.json`: its wave's module and
  the wave and batch indices
- `objective` — `wrap` or `port`; `pass` — `first` for a translation batch, `review` for a
  review batch; `Σ first` / `Σ review` total each pass apart
- `types` / `symbols` / `fields` — the batch's scheduled units (callbacks count as
  symbols) and its types' assigned field accessors; a review row counts what it reviewed
- `$` / `tokens` / `wall` — the agent's computed cost (API-equivalent under
  subscription), its tokens in millions as `crustify usage` reports them, and its elapsed
  time, C rebuild included; `$/<unit>` divides `$` by the row's units
- `+LoC` — the landing's Rust insertions/deletions; `loc` — its `.rs` insertions
- `cov (C/Rust)` — line coverage after the landing, all test workloads in one run: C over
  the link unit's TUs, Rust over non-test sources; a `Σ` cell is the pass's last landing
- `+UB safe tests` … `+unit tests` — the tests the landing added, with its C/Rust coverage
  change in pp
- `+lifecycle` … `+misc`, `total` — the reports a review batch filed, by kind
- safety audit columns — the Safety audit's metrics, as a landing changed them
- API stability columns — the landing's items by how `ffimap api` classifies their consumer-facing API against its base: `kept`, `extended`, `changed`, `removed`, `new`, and `→Replaces` for the anchors a port moved; `unattributed` the crate's public items no anchor reaches, by module; `reasons` the changed and removed items with the reason the batch recorded
- `cost` / `review cost` / `total` — a module's translation, review and combined cost;
  `module wall` — first launch to final gate; `Σ recorded agents` leaves the assistant
  out, `Σ campaign` adds it, without per-unit cells
- `UB safe tests` … `Unit tests` — `#[test]` functions per suite, each with the coverage of
  running it alone; `Total tests` — all four, whose coverage is one joint run's union,
  never the sum
- `total`, `ported` and `wrapped` types and symbols — the scheduled public-API units, and
  those with a `Replaces:` or a `Wraps:` anchor at the tip; `share` is of the total

Every table below is a heading, a model line and the table. All prose belongs
in Notes.

### Reading the batch tables

Batch rows from every sub-campaign share one table per route; the `module` cell names the
row's sub-campaign as `<link-unit>/<module>`, the same name as its Overview row.
Every type row is a `wrap` batch: the rows the wrap campaign landed, kept in the `Types`
tables' `objective` column since the template merged its wrap and port tables. A `wavefront` report category, for ownership findings the review resubmitted, is
counted under `+misc`.

Each batch is measured on two tree states: just before its first landing commit (the wave
base or the previous batch's landing) and its last landing commit. `cov (C/Rust)` is the
latter, from one instrumented build per state: the four workloads (`--lib` unit tests,
`ub_safe`, `ub_unsafe`, `equiv`) each run alone into their own profile directory against
the `coverage` prebuild, and their union is the cell. C is lcov line coverage over the 196
translation units `libgit2.so` links, with a zero baseline from the `.gcno` files so that
untouched TUs count; Rust is cargo-llvm-cov line coverage over `crustify/rust/libgit2`'s
non-`tests/` sources, minus every line inside a `#[cfg(test)]` item (the inline unit-test
modules). All workloads share one denominator, and the union is the union of their covered
lines. Every Rust cell and Rust delta in these tables was restated on 2026-10-12. The
earlier figures counted those test lines, 60% of the instrumented lines at the
`libgit2/index` tip, which held the integration suites' coverage far down and credited
the unit tests for running themselves. All 182 recorded states were re-measured; the C
cells and C deltas stay as first recorded. The eight `libgit2/config` states between
`beeda6a07` and the export revert `c5440d3ee` call the two reverted constructors, so they
were measured against a private coverage build of their own source, which exports them. A Σ `cov` cell is the state after the table's chronologically
last landing. The `(+C/+Rust pp)` pairs in the `…: tests` tables are each workload's own
coverage after minus before, so a batch that adds code its workload does not reach shows a
negative Rust delta. The safety audit deltas are the Safety audit's metrics over the same two
states, from the scans the `ffimap` skill names; the tables hold no row from before the
metrics were redefined, as `Safety audit metrics from ffimap's counter tree` describes.

Test counts are `#[test]` functions the landing commits add, by directory; trybuild
`compile_fail` cases are not counted. `+LoC` and `rv loc` count `.rs` lines under
`crustify/rust/`, so review reproducer crates under `crustify/reviews/` are excluded. The
measurement scripts live outside the repository, beside the orchestrator's other helpers;
each batch's `ffimap.json` beside it is the unseeded scan of its last landing commit.

### Overview test counts

The Coverage stats test lines were measured again on 2026-11-04, at `crustify/devel`
`1e732ebff`, with the testing spec's Coverage method, which replaces the gcov one the
earlier figures used. Those figures are not comparable with these. Each count is the
number of tests its compiled test binary registers (`-- --list`): `--lib` for the unit
tests, one of them ignored, and the `ub_safe`, `ub_unsafe` and `equiv` integration crates.
The trybuild runner is one `ub_safe` test, and it was skipped in the coverage run since it
runs no code. `ub_safe` holds 688 tests since the unsafe fixtures were removed. Doctests
are not counted in the table.

The `coverage` variant, `build.json` version 4, and the side libraries' `coverage`
installs (version 3 of each) compile the C with clang 23,
`-fprofile-instr-generate -fcoverage-mapping`. The Rust is a scratch copy under
`crustify/tmp/coverage/` with `#[coverage(off)]` on every test item, compiled on
`nightly-2026-10-08` (LLVM 23) with `-C instrument-coverage`. Each suite ran alone into
its own profile, and `Total tests` is the merge of the four suites' profiles, their union.
Every figure is the `TOTAL` line of the nightly's `llvm-cov report`, with `libgit2.so` and
every test binary as objects for every suite.

- C is line coverage over the 86,770 lines `libgit2.so` maps to `c/src/libgit2`,
  `c/src/util`, `c/include` and the bundled `c/deps` it compiles (`llhttp`, `ntlmclient`,
  `reftable`, `xdiff`). The generated headers and the C's own tests count toward none.
  libgit2 proper, `src/` and `include/` without `deps/`, is `52.42`% of 68,023 lines. The
  total covers `61.63`% of functions and `47.65`% of regions.
- Rust is line coverage over the 13,226 lines of the crate's 42 files under `src/`, with
  `tests/`, the `-sys` crate and dependencies left out by path. The total covers `99.02`% of
  functions and `97.65`% of regions.
- Doctests, run as a suite of their own: 347, of which 346 pass under the nightly. The
  compile-fail doctest on `CommitBuilder` expects `E0624`, which stable reports and the
  nightly does not; it passes on plain. They reach `11.94`% of C lines and `23.30`% of
  Rust lines, and add no line to the four suites' union.

`crustify/scripts/coverage/` holds the scripts that measured them:
`run.sh "$PWD" libgit2 "$PWD/crustify/tmp/coverage"`, then
`report.py crustify/tmp/coverage "C=$PWD/c/src/libgit2:$PWD/c/src/util:$PWD/c/include:$PWD/c/deps,Rust=$PWD/crustify/tmp/coverage/tree/src" --c crustify/builds/coverage/libgit2.so.1.9.0`.

The UB suites also run under ASan+UBSan, TSan, Miri and BorrowSanitizer in the agents'
gates. Those runs share one test set and are not counted again.

- API stability columns — the landing's items by how `ffimap api` classifies their consumer-facing API against its base: `kept`, `extended`, `changed`, `removed`, `new`, and `→Replaces` for the anchors a port moved; `unattributed` the crate's public items no anchor reaches, by module; `reasons` the changed and removed items with the reason the batch recorded
- `cost` / `review cost` / `total` — a module's translation, review and combined cost;
  `module wall` — first launch to final gate; `Σ recorded agents` leaves the assistant
  out, `Σ campaign` adds it, without per-unit cells
- `UB safe tests` … `Unit tests` — `#[test]` functions per suite, each with the coverage of
  running it alone; `Total tests` — all four, whose coverage is one joint run's union,
  never the sum
- `total`, `ported` and `wrapped` types and symbols — the scheduled public-API units, and
  those with a `Replaces:` or a `Wraps:` anchor at the tip; `share` is of the total

Every table below is a heading, a model line and the table. All prose belongs
in Notes.

### Reading the batch tables

Batch rows from every sub-campaign share one table per route; the `module` cell names the
row's sub-campaign as `<link-unit>/<module>`, the same name as its Overview row.
Every type row is a `wrap` batch: the rows the wrap campaign landed, kept in the `Types`
tables' `objective` column since the template merged its wrap and port tables. A `wavefront` report category, for ownership findings the review resubmitted, is
counted under `+misc`.

Each batch is measured on two tree states: just before its first landing commit (the wave
base or the previous batch's landing) and its last landing commit. `cov (C/Rust)` is the
latter, from one instrumented build per state: the four workloads (`--lib` unit tests,
`ub_safe`, `ub_unsafe`, `equiv`) each run alone into their own profile directory against
the `coverage` prebuild, and their union is the cell. C is lcov line coverage over the 196
translation units `libgit2.so` links, with a zero baseline from the `.gcno` files so that
untouched TUs count; Rust is cargo-llvm-cov line coverage over `crustify/rust/libgit2`'s
non-`tests/` sources, minus every line inside a `#[cfg(test)]` item (the inline unit-test
modules). All workloads share one denominator, and the union is the union of their covered
lines. Every Rust cell and Rust delta in these tables was restated on 2026-10-12. The
earlier figures counted those test lines, 60% of the instrumented lines at the
`libgit2/index` tip, which held the integration suites' coverage far down and credited
the unit tests for running themselves. All 182 recorded states were re-measured; the C
cells and C deltas stay as first recorded. The eight `libgit2/config` states between
`beeda6a07` and the export revert `c5440d3ee` call the two reverted constructors, so they
were measured against a private coverage build of their own source, which exports them. A Σ `cov` cell is the state after the table's chronologically
last landing. The `(+C/+Rust pp)` pairs in the `…: tests` tables are each workload's own
coverage after minus before, so a batch that adds code its workload does not reach shows a
negative Rust delta. The safety audit deltas are the Safety audit's metrics over the same two
states, from the scans the `ffimap` skill names; the tables hold no row from before the
metrics were redefined, as `Safety audit metrics from ffimap's counter tree` describes.

Test counts are `#[test]` functions the landing commits add, by directory; trybuild
`compile_fail` cases are not counted. `+LoC` and `rv loc` count `.rs` lines under
`crustify/rust/`, so review reproducer crates under `crustify/reviews/` are excluded. The
measurement scripts live outside the repository, beside the orchestrator's other helpers;
each batch's `ffimap.json` beside it is the unseeded scan of its last landing commit.

### Overview test counts

The Coverage stats test lines were measured again on 2026-11-04, at `crustify/devel`
`1e732ebff`, with the testing spec's Coverage method, which replaces the gcov one the
earlier figures used. Those figures are not comparable with these. Each count is the
number of tests its compiled test binary registers (`-- --list`): `--lib` for the unit
tests, one of them ignored, and the `ub_safe`, `ub_unsafe` and `equiv` integration crates.
The trybuild runner is one `ub_safe` test, and it was skipped in the coverage run since it
runs no code. `ub_safe` holds 688 tests since the unsafe fixtures were removed. Doctests
are not counted in the table.

The `coverage` variant, `build.json` version 4, and the side libraries' `coverage`
installs (version 3 of each) compile the C with clang 23,
`-fprofile-instr-generate -fcoverage-mapping`. The Rust is a scratch copy under
`crustify/tmp/coverage/` with `#[coverage(off)]` on every test item, compiled on
`nightly-2026-10-08` (LLVM 23) with `-C instrument-coverage`. Each suite ran alone into
its own profile, and `Total tests` is the merge of the four suites' profiles, their union.
Every figure is the `TOTAL` line of the nightly's `llvm-cov report`, with `libgit2.so` and
every test binary as objects for every suite.

- C is line coverage over the 86,770 lines `libgit2.so` maps to `c/src/libgit2`,
  `c/src/util`, `c/include` and the bundled `c/deps` it compiles (`llhttp`, `ntlmclient`,
  `reftable`, `xdiff`). The generated headers and the C's own tests count toward none.
  libgit2 proper, `src/` and `include/` without `deps/`, is `52.42`% of 68,023 lines. The
  total covers `61.63`% of functions and `47.65`% of regions.

  functions and `97.65`% of regions.

  nightly does not; it passes on plain. They reach `11.94`% of C lines and `23.30`% of
  Rust lines, and add no line to the four suites' union.

`crustify/scripts/coverage/` holds the scripts that measured them:
`run.sh "$PWD" libgit2 "$PWD/crustify/tmp/coverage"`, then
`report.py crustify/tmp/coverage "C=$PWD/c/src/libgit2:$PWD/c/src/util:$PWD/c/include:$PWD/c/deps,Rust=$PWD/crustify/tmp/coverage/tree/src" --c crustify/builds/coverage/libgit2.so.1.9.0`.

gates. Those runs share one test set and are not counted again.

The module pass, and the module's only review, over batch 0's three paths (`680ac73bf`), for
every objective with `fix`. The module files no finding of its own. `decode_char`,
`char_count` and `valid_prefix_len` are `git_utf8_iterate`'s, `git_utf8_char_length`'s and
`git_utf8_valid_buf_length`'s results for every input but `str_len` 0, where C reads past
its size and the port refuses, as its docs and a unit test say. The class table is
utf8proc's, and the anchors, homes and placement follow the conventions. The ownership
store's pointer blocks for the four functions hold against the C. `test_utf8__char_length`'s
ten assertions are all carried over, unchanged, by `char_count_carries_over_the_c_test`, so
no case of the module's one C test is left uncarried. That test uses only the module's
exports, so it stays after the switch.

The gateway was reviewed for what the C that stays relies on. `next_hfs_char` needs a
length no larger than `*len` and the code point written. `git_xdiff_cb` needs a prefix no
longer than its header, cut before a sequence its size splits, and `fs_path.c` needs the
count. None passes `str_len` 0. The exports keep each, and a panic cannot unwind into C.
The export feature on, `fmt` and `clippy --all-targets` pass with warnings denied. With the
exports linked in place of C's `utf8.o`, the whole workspace passes on `plain` and passes
under ASan+UBSan but for the known nightly failures. That link used a private build under
`crustify/tmp/`, whose copy of the archive lacks `utf8.c.o`, named by `CRUSTIFY_BUILD_DIR`.
`nm` shows no `utf8proc_utf8class`, and `next_hfs_char` and `git_xdiff_cb` call Rust. As a
scratch check, C's own suites ran too: the variant's `libgit2_tests` and `util_tests` were
relinked from their `build.ninja` edges, against the crate built as a `staticlib` with the
feature, in place of `src/util`'s `utf8.c.o`. `util_tests` passed whole, `-sutf8` included.
`libgit2_tests -spath -sdiff -sindex -scheckout -srefs` matched the stock binary: 825
passed, 22 skipped. That procedure is proposed for the `port` batches' gates
(`crustify/evolution/export-link-check`). The gateway had no test (`test-adequacy`): its
region gains four `unit_priv` tests, which compile with it, under the feature until the
switch. They check the code point and length written or the refusal's 0 and -1, a
`next_hfs_char` walk, the two counts, and that `str_len` 0 reads nothing, NULL or dangling.
Each input sits in an allocation of exactly its size. The four pass on `plain`, under
ASan+UBSan with the exports linked, and under Miri. Two mutants fail them: `bytes()`
reading one byte more fails under Miri, and a refusal writing `u32::MAX` fails the
assertions. `git_utf8_iterate`'s `# Safety` now asks for an aligned `out`.

The module's end gates found the pass's one finding, outside the module:
`ub_safe/first-filter-loads-race-on-builtin-filter-flags`. TSan failed `lib` on the tip with
libgit2's `filter_initialize` race. A `checkout` fixture staged files through
`git_index_add_bypath` while a `blob` test initialised the filters. libgit2 writes a filter's
`initialized` flag under only its registry's read lock, and the crate closed that for
`filter.rs`'s constructors alone. A `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` reproducer races two threads'
`hash_file` calls and exits 66, five runs of five. The fix has `runtime_pinned`, which every
safe constructor passes, call `initialise_builtin_filters`. The helper now only looks `crlf`
and `ident` up, which initialises them without allocating. A first version kept its scratch
list, and the list's 145 and 192 bytes failed eleven allocator-tracing `equiv` tests. The
reproducer exits 0, and its regression test, `ub_safe`'s
`filter::first_loads_on_two_threads_do_not_race`, fails under TSan without the call. Its
`disclosure.md` is for libgit2's issue tracker. Filing a gate's true positive outside the
workset is proposed for `reviewing` (`crustify/evolution/gate-findings-outside-the-workset`,
crustify `1423c7f`, awaiting review).

Gates ran on `end-gates` snapshots under the worktree's `crustify/tmp/`, at 24 jobs, without
BSan (the settings' `sanitizers` answer). On the tip `680ac73bf`: plain passes the whole
workspace (`lib` 844 and 1 ignored, `equiv` 534, `ub_safe` 762, `ub_unsafe` 120, `unit_pub`
78, `hidden_symbols` 1, doctests 75 and 378). ASan+UBSan passes it but for the known
`compile_fail` snapshots and `CommitBuilder` doctest. TSan fails those and `lib`, with the
race above. Miri passes every binary (`lib` 396, `ub_safe` 194, `equiv` 38, `unit_pub` 43,
`ub_unsafe` 19 passed, the rest marked). On the landed tree, plain passes the whole
workspace, `ub_safe` 763. ASan+UBSan and TSan pass it but for the known failures, `lib`
included under TSan. Miri passes every binary as on the tip, `ub_safe`'s new test marked (`calls libgit2`).

Coverage: `run.sh` on a `git archive` of the tip and on this tree, read with `report.py` from
each scratch tree's `src/libgit2`, the unit column merging `lib` and `unit_pub`. The totals
move from `44.99`% / `98.81`% on the tip to `44.98`% / `98.82`%. The tip measures `44.99`%,
where batch 0 recorded `44.97`% for the same tree, so each suite's shift of a few hundredths
is within run-to-run variation. The first pin's filter lookups add C lines to every suite.
The gateway's tests compile out with the feature off, so the worklist's figures are batch
0's, and its tests count `+0`. The safety audit scan (ffimap `9aa2ef1`, batch 0's flags, the
export feature on) differs from batch 0's in `FFI calls` and `unsafe blocks` `-3` each,
which are the scratch list's three calls. The Overview's LoC moves by `code.loc.total` (`-2`)
and `code.tests.loc.total` (`+114`). `ffimap api` over the worklist: the three functions are
`kept`, the table and `utf8_charlen` `missing`, every unattributed module `kept`. No raw
binding or C changed, so the packaging gate does not apply. Usage cells are the
assistant's.

#!/bin/bash
# run.sh <repo> <package> <cov dir>: build a coverage-instrumented scratch copy of the safe
# crate against the `coverage` variant, its test items under #[coverage(off)], and run each
# suite alone into <cov dir>/prof/<suite>: lib, each integration test binary, and doc. Each
# binary links the variant's C statically, so its profiles count the C and the Rust alike.
# report.py then reads the figures (testing spec, Coverage), with the variant's static archive
# as the C object.
set -euo pipefail
repo=$1 pkg=$2 out=$3
host=x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
nightly=$(sed -n 's/^nightly = "\(.*\)"$/\1/p' "$repo/Cargo.toml")
tree=$out/tree
rm -rf "$out"; mkdir -p "$tree/crustify" "$out/prof"
(cd "$repo" && tar -cf - --exclude=./target --exclude=./crustify --exclude=./c --exclude=./.git .) | (cd "$tree" && tar -xf -)
ln -s "$repo/c" "$tree/c"
ln -s "$repo/crustify/artifacts" "$tree/crustify/artifacts"
ln -s "$repo/crustify/builds" "$tree/crustify/builds"
python3 "$(dirname "$0")/mark.py" "$tree/src" "$tree/src/lib.rs"
cd "$tree"
export CRUSTIFY_BUILD_VARIANT=coverage CARGO_TARGET_DIR=$out/target
export RUSTFLAGS="-C instrument-coverage" RUSTDOCFLAGS="-C instrument-coverage -Z unstable-options --persist-doctests $out/doctests"
cargo "+$nightly" test -p "$pkg" --target $host --no-run --message-format=json 2>"$out/build.err" \
  | python3 -c 'import sys,json
for l in sys.stdin:
  try: d=json.loads(l)
  except: continue
  if d.get("reason")=="compiler-artifact" and d.get("executable") and d["target"]["kind"]!=["custom-build"] and d.get("profile",{}).get("test"): print(d["target"]["name"],d["target"]["kind"][0],d["executable"])' > "$out/bins.txt"
cat "$out/bins.txt"
while read -r name kind exe; do
  suite=$([ "$kind" = lib ] && echo lib || echo "$name")
  mkdir -p "$out/prof/$suite"
  echo "== $suite"
  LLVM_PROFILE_FILE="$out/prof/$suite/%p-%m.profraw" "$exe" --skip compile_fail > "$out/$suite.log" 2>&1 || echo "rc=$? in $suite"
  tail -3 "$out/$suite.log"

done < "$out/bins.txt"

# A `ub_unsafe` fixture calls an api.c function that has no export, unlinking the suite at the switch

- **finding**: `misc/ub-unsafe-fixture-calls-an-unexported-api-function`
- **batch**: `wave-194/batch-6/run-1`, the `symbol` review of `deps/llhttp/api.c`'s folded
  waves
- **items**: `fn::llhttp_set_error_reason`, ported by `wave-194/batch-3` (`2a51ccb3f`) as
  `ParserMut::set_reason` and not exported, since no C outside api.c calls it; the test
  `ub_unsafe`'s `deps::llhttp::llhttp::set_settings_ptr::a_reason_its_callbacks_set_is_read_while_the_parser_holds_it`
  (`wave-194/batch-5`, `f58d38aa9`)
- **affected commit**: `b3d6b9b37`
- **files**: `tests/ub_unsafe/deps/llhttp/llhttp.rs`

## Finding

Once api.c switches from C, `api.c.o` leaves the variants' archives and the gateway's 31
exports are all that define api.c's symbols. Every suite but `equiv`, whose comparisons call
api.c's C by design and retire with it, must then link against the exports alone.
`wave-194/batch-4` checked that with private builds whose archive copy lacked `api.c.o`, and
moved two fixtures off `llhttp_settings_init`, which has no export. Its link check ran before
its rebase onto `f58d38aa9`, which added batch 5's regression test, so it did not see that
test's fixture `refuse_url`, a C-style `on_url` that stores its reason through
`sys::llhttp_set_error_reason`. With the archive lacking `api.c.o` and the export feature on,
`ub_unsafe` does not link:

```text
rust-lld: error: undefined symbol: llhttp_set_error_reason
>>> referenced by llhttp.rs:292 (tests/ub_unsafe/deps/llhttp/llhttp.rs:292)
>>>               …/ub_unsafe-a7f69842e392650b…rcgu.o:(ub_unsafe::deps::llhttp::llhttp::set_settings_ptr::refuse_url)
>>> did you mean: llhttp_get_error_reason
error: could not compile `libgit2-crustify` (test "ub_unsafe") due to 1 previous error
```

So api.c's switch, whose gates link every suite against the exports, would fail on it. No
other suite but `equiv` calls an api.c function without an export: the remaining `sys::`
calls outside `equiv` are `llhttp_init` and `llhttp_execute`, both exported, and
`llhttp__internal_init` and `llhttp__internal_execute`, llhttp.c's.

## Reproducer

Not a UB, equivalence or logic finding, so the evidence is the link check itself. On
`b3d6b9b37`, from the repository root, with a scratch copy of the `plain` variant's build
whose archive lacks `api.c.o` (each entry of `crustify/builds/plain` linked into
`crustify/tmp/linkcheck/plain` but `crustify/libcrustify.a`, copied and then
`ar d crustify/libcrustify.a api.c.o`, 211 objects):

```
CRUSTIFY_BUILD_DIR=$PWD/crustify/tmp/linkcheck/plain \
CARGO_TARGET_DIR=$PWD/crustify/tmp/target-linkcheck-plain \
crustify/scripts/cargo-variant.sh plain test --features ffi-export-deps-llhttp-api-c \
    --lib --test ub_safe --test ub_unsafe --test unit_pub --test hidden_symbols
```

It fails with the error above.

## Fix

In this batch's second commit, `refuse_url` stores the reason as `llhttp_set_error_reason`'s
body does, `(*parser).reason = reason`, a C callback's own write to the field, which keeps the
test's scenario (a C callback setting a reason its context owns) and needs no api.c symbol.
The link check above then passes on `plain` and on `asan-ubsan`, every suite but `equiv`.

# `llhttp_execute`'s export moves an empty run's error position off `data`

- **finding**: `equiv/execute-export-moves-an-empty-runs-error-pos`
- **batch**: `wave-194/batch-7/run-1`, `deps/llhttp/api.c`'s module pass
- **items**: `fn::llhttp_execute`'s export under `ffi-export-deps-llhttp-api-c`, which serves
  `transports/httpparser.c`'s `git_http_parser_execute` once api.c switches from C
- **affected commit**: `9124cc5a6` (the export since `2a51ccb3f`)
- **files**: `src/libgit2/deps/llhttp/api.rs`

## Finding

api.c's `llhttp_execute(parser, data, len)` is `llhttp__internal_execute(parser, data,
data + len)`. The generated parser restarts a span the previous run left open at `data`, hands
the span's callback the run from there to `data + len`, and, when the callback refuses it,
stores `data + len` as the parser's `error_pos` (`llhttp.c`, `llhttp__internal_execute`).
`llhttp.h` documents that position as "relative to the `data` argument of
`llhttp_execute()`", and `git_http_parser_execute` computes its parsed length as
`llhttp_get_error_pos(parser) - data` (`c/src/libgit2/transports/httpparser.c:118`).

The export read a run of 0 bytes as `&[]` whatever `data` was:

```rust
let bytes: &[u8] = if len == 0 { &[] } else { unsafe { slice::from_raw_parts(data.cast::<u8>(), len) } };
```

An empty slice's address is the dangling `0x1`, so `parse` handed C the range `0x1..0x1`. When a
run of 0 bytes ends a header's name the previous run left open, and the name's callback refuses
it, the export leaves `error_pos` at `0x1`, where C leaves it at `data`. `error_pos - data` is
then no offset into the run. Its other doc line claimed C's `data + len` allows a NULL `data`,
which C does not: `NULL + 0` is undefined in C17.

libgit2's C does not reach this today: `git_http_parser_execute` calls `llhttp_finish`, not
`llhttp_execute`, for a run of 0 bytes. The export still keeps C's contract for every caller,
and the module's equivalence tests compared the safe `execute`, which takes a slice, never the
export.

## Reproducer

`Cargo.toml` and `src/main.rs` beside this report. It runs two parsers alike, one through the
export and one through api.c's body, `llhttp__internal_execute(parser, data, data + len)`, and
compares their returns and error positions. It links the export in place of api.c's C, so it
needs a build whose archive lacks `api.c.o`: from the repository root, each entry of
`crustify/builds/plain` symlinked into `crustify/tmp/linkcheck/plain` but
`crustify/libcrustify.a`, which is copied and then `ar d crustify/libcrustify.a api.c.o`
(211 objects). From this directory:

```
W=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)
side=$(realpath -m "$W/crustify/builds/plain/../../../..")
CRUSTIFY_BUILD_VARIANT=plain CRUSTIFY_BUILD_DIR="$W/crustify/tmp/linkcheck/plain" \
PKG_CONFIG_PATH="$side/pcre2-bindings/crustify/builds/plain/install/lib/pkgconfig" \
cargo run -q
```

On `9124cc5a6` it exits 101 (`run-affected.log`):

```text
llhttp_execute: 7, api.c's body: 7
error_pos: export 0x1, api.c's body 0x7fffefa54091, data 0x7fffefa54091
```

# `llhttp_execute`'s export moves an empty run's error position off `data`

- **finding**: `equiv/execute-export-moves-an-empty-runs-error-pos`

- **files**: `src/libgit2/deps/llhttp/api.rs`

## Finding

api.c's `llhttp_execute(parser, data, len)` is `llhttp__internal_execute(parser, data,
data + len)`. The generated parser restarts a span the previous run left open at `data`, hands
the span's callback the run from there to `data + len`, and, when the callback refuses it,
stores `data + len` as the parser's `error_pos` (`llhttp.c`, `llhttp__internal_execute`).
`llhttp.h` documents that position as "relative to the `data` argument of
`llhttp_execute()`", and `git_http_parser_execute` computes its parsed length as
`llhttp_get_error_pos(parser) - data` (`c/src/libgit2/transports/httpparser.c:118`).

The export read a run of 0 bytes as `&[]` whatever `data` was:

```rust
let bytes: &[u8] = if len == 0 { &[] } else { unsafe { slice::from_raw_parts(data.cast::<u8>(), len) } };
```

An empty slice's address is the dangling `0x1`, so `parse` handed C the range `0x1..0x1`. When a
run of 0 bytes ends a header's name the previous run left open, and the name's callback refuses
it, the export leaves `error_pos` at `0x1`, where C leaves it at `data`. `error_pos - data` is
then no offset into the run. Its other doc line claimed C's `data + len` allows a NULL `data`,
which C does not: `NULL + 0` is undefined in C17.

`llhttp_execute`, for a run of 0 bytes. The export still keeps C's contract for every caller,
and the module's equivalence tests compared the safe `execute`, which takes a slice, never the
export.
